function: DQN controls LEO satellites: centre-frequency beam direction, DA-IRS element delay and phase, and subcarrier-to-grid assignment, to minimize long-term communication latency (p. 6).
system: Two LEO satellites at 800 km, one transmitter and a 1024-element reflecting DA-IRS with delay elements each; OFDMA, three subcarriers, 10.5 GHz centre, 0.25 GHz bandwidth (p. 9).
method: DQN with policy and target networks (double-Q update) and prioritized replay; 4 1D-conv plus 4 fully connected layers; reinforcement learning trained offline at the NOC (pp. 7-9).
data_channel: Custom simulation: g all-ones, rain and distance attenuation, two satellites over 10 grids, truncated-normal request demand; no standard channel model or public dataset (p. 9).
test_conditions: Trained on 1 million episodes; average delay evaluated while sweeping Mmax, demand variance and total demand; no separate unseen scenario stated (pp. 9-11).
baselines: Comp 1: DQN trained for instantaneous rate (discount 0); Comp 2: trained model without frequency prism; both are variants of the proposed method, no non-learned baseline (p. 9).
metrics: Average delay time (latency = beam-control switches times 12 s interval) versus Mmax, demand variance and total demand (pp. 3, 10-11).
complexity: none; only qualitative remarks that training cost grows with the number of satellites (pp. 6, 12).
q1_support: p. 9: "we considered the vector g to be an all-ones vector"; the channel is a custom model with rain and distance attenuation (p. 4). No 3GPP, DeepMIMO or measured data is named.
q2_support: p. 9: "trained on a dataset comprising 1 million episodes"; p. 10: "systematically varying the variance in the initial communication demand distribution". Sweeps of demand statistics only; no statement of training on one scenario and testing on another.
q3_support: p. 9: "As a variant of the proposed method, the instantaneous rate optimization method (referred to as Comp 1)"; "(denoted as Comp 2) operates under a model trained on the same 1 million episodes". Both are learned variants; no non-learned method and no earlier published learned method.
q4_support: p. 3: "facilitating efficient control determination with minimal computational overhead"; p. 12: "substantially elevating the computational cost of training". Qualitative only; no order of complexity, FLOPs, parameter count or runtime.
q5_support: p. 9: "trained on a dataset comprising 1 million episodes" is a simulated set of episodes. The paper gives no code or data link, no DOI and uses no public channel dataset.
notes: Borderline on above_phy: the DQN state is the per-grid demand, but its actions are beam direction, DA-IRS delay and subcarrier assignment, which the instructions treat as physical layer in satellite links (p. 6). Area 6 wins over 3 by the order of specificity. The abstract cites traditional single-beam control, but Section IV defines only Comp 1 and Comp 2, both trained models (p. 9). Table II was read from the page image (p. 9). Reviewer may check whether one trained model is reused across Figs. 8-9 (pp. 10-11), which would bear on q2.
